title: Governance, Board Reporting and Supervisory Engagement
summary: Brings the programme together into a governance and reporting model for quantum readiness: accountability, board information, assurance and the evidence the firm should be able to show the authority.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: Brings the programme together into a governance and reporting model for quantum readiness: accountability, board information, assurance and the evidence the firm should be able to show the authority.
Learning Objectives: Allocate accountability for quantum readiness across the three lines of defence
Specify the management information and assurance the board needs
Prepare the evidence of quantum readiness that supervisors will expect
Syllabus: Ownership, steering groups and the role of internal audit
Board reporting: inventory coverage, milestones, exceptions and dependencies
International work: BIS, G7 Cyber Expert Group and national cyber agencies
Workshop: the firm's quantum readiness plan and board paper
Intended Audience: Chief information security officers, chief technology officers, architects and security engineering leads
Operational resilience, technology risk, third-party risk and internal audit staff
Senior managers and programme sponsors accountable for cyber, data protection and change
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of information security, technology risk or operational resilience is helpful. No knowledge of quantum physics or cryptographic mathematics is required.
Core Reading: NIST, FIPS 203, 204 and 205: Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards (2024)
G7 Cyber Expert Group, Public Statement on Planning for the Opportunities and Risks of Quantum Computing (2024)
FSB, Enhancing Third-Party Risk Management and Oversight: A Toolkit for Financial Institutions and Financial Authorities (2023)
